explain.es: En B1 viste will y going to. En C1 el futuro se vuelve más preciso: nos situamos en un punto concreto del futuro y miramos qué estará pasando (future continuous), qué habrá terminado (future perfect) o cuánto tiempo llevará ocurriendo algo (future perfect continuous). Además, el inglés tiene expresiones para lo inminente o programado (be about to, be due to, be on the point of) y formas para hablar del futuro visto desde el pasado (was going to, would, was to), imprescindibles en narración y en registro formal.
explain.en: At C1 the future becomes more precise: we stand at a point in the future and look at what will be in progress, what will have finished, or how long something will have been going on. We also express imminence and schedules, and the future seen from the past.

explain.title: 1 · Future continuous
explain.title_en: Actions in progress in the future
explain.es: Se forma con will be + -ing. Lo usamos para: (a) una acción en curso en un momento concreto del futuro (this time tomorrow, at 9 tonight); (b) algo que ocurrirá en el curso normal de los acontecimientos, sin intención especial (I'll be seeing him at the conference anyway); (c) preguntar con cortesía por los planes de alguien: Will you be using the car tonight? suena más educado que Will you use…?, que puede sonar a petición o a presión.
explain.en: will be + -ing: an action in progress at a future moment; something that will happen in the normal course of events; polite questions about someone's plans.

examples.en: This time next week I'll be lying on a beach in Menorca.
examples.es: La semana que viene a estas horas estaré tumbado en una playa de Menorca.

examples.en: Don't ring at eight — we'll be having dinner.
examples.es: No llames a las ocho: estaremos cenando.

examples.en: Will you be using the meeting room this afternoon?
examples.es: ¿Vas a usar la sala de reuniones esta tarde? (pregunta cortés)

examples.en: I'll be passing the chemist's anyway — shall I pick up your prescription?
examples.es: Voy a pasar por la farmacia de todos modos: ¿te recojo la receta?

explain.title: 2 · Future perfect simple
explain.es: Se forma con will have + participio. Expresa una acción que estará terminada antes de un momento del futuro. Casi siempre va con by (para, como muy tarde): by Friday, by then, by the end of the year, by the time + presente. Ojo: by marca un límite, mientras que until marca duración (hasta). También sirve para hacer suposiciones sobre el presente: You'll have heard the news (ya te habrás enterado).
explain.en: will have + past participle: completed before a point in the future, usually with by. It can also express an assumption about the present: You'll have heard the news.

examples.en: By the time you read this email, I'll have left the company.
examples.es: Para cuando leas este correo, ya habré dejado la empresa.

examples.en: The committee won't have reached a decision by Monday.
examples.es: El comité no habrá tomado una decisión para el lunes.

examples.en: Will they have finished the renovation before the summer?
examples.es: ¿Habrán terminado la reforma antes del verano?

examples.en: You'll have heard that Marta has been promoted.
examples.es: Ya te habrás enterado de que han ascendido a Marta.

explain.title: 3 · Future perfect continuous
explain.title_en: Duration up to a future point
explain.es: Se forma con will have been + -ing. Pone el foco en la duración de una actividad hasta un momento del futuro, normalmente con for + periodo. En español solemos decir llevaré… años o hará… que. Recuerda: los verbos de estado (know, own, believe, be) no van en forma continua: By June I'll have known her for twenty years.
explain.en: will have been + -ing: focuses on duration up to a future point, typically with for. State verbs use the future perfect simple instead.

examples.en: Next month I'll have been working here for a decade.
examples.es: El mes que viene llevaré una década trabajando aquí.

examples.en: By the time we land, we'll have been travelling for almost twenty hours.
examples.es: Cuando aterricemos, llevaremos casi veinte horas viajando.

examples.en: In 2027 the observatory will have been collecting data for half a century.
examples.es: En 2027 el observatorio llevará medio siglo recopilando datos.

explain.title: Las formas de un vistazo
explain.title_en: The future forms at a glance
head: Forma · Form
Estructura
Idea clave
Marcadores
Ejemplo
rows: en curso en un momento futuro
terminado antes de un momento futuro
by Friday, by then, by the time…
By 8 I'll have been driving for 3 hours.
Quick — the bus is about to leave!
The plane is due to land at 6.40.
explain.note: Truco: at + hora → en curso (continuous). by + hora → terminado (perfect). for + periodo hasta un momento → duración (perfect continuous).
explain.note_en: at + time → in progress; by + time → completed; for + period → duration.

explain.title: AT las 8, BY las 8 o FOR… hasta las 8
explain.es: Imagina una línea del tiempo: el mismo verbo cambia de forma según miremos el momento, el límite o la duración.
explain.en: Same verb, three perspectives: the moment, the deadline or the duration.

cols.head: 🎞️ at 8 pm · en curso
items: At 8 pm I'll be writing the report.
A las 8 estaré escribiendo el informe.
Estaré en plena acción.

cols.head: 🏁 by 8 pm · terminado
items: By 8 pm I'll have written the report.
Para las 8 habré escrito el informe.
La acción ya habrá acabado.

cols.head: ⏱️ for 3 hours · duración
items: By 8 pm I'll have been writing it for three hours.
A las 8 llevaré tres horas escribiéndolo.
Importa cuánto dura.

explain.title: 4 · Inminente o previsto
explain.es: be about to + infinitivo = estar a punto de: algo inminente. No admite expresiones de tiempo (about to leave in two hours), pero sí just: I was just about to ring you. be on the point of + -ing significa lo mismo con un tono más formal o dramático. be on the verge / brink of + nombre o -ing = al borde de (crisis, éxito, extinción). be due to + infinitivo = estar previsto según un horario o calendario; sí admite hora o fecha. En prensa verás be set to (se prevé que) y be to (está previsto que, anuncios oficiales).
explain.en: be about to (imminent, no time expression), be on the point of + -ing (more formal), be on the verge of (on the edge of), be due to (scheduled, takes a time), be set to / be to (news and official announcements).

examples.en: Please switch off your phones — the performance is about to begin.
examples.es: Apaguen los móviles, por favor: la función está a punto de empezar.

examples.en: The two firms are on the point of signing a merger agreement.
examples.es: Las dos empresas están a punto de firmar un acuerdo de fusión.

examples.en: The report is due to be published on 15 March.
examples.es: Está previsto que el informe se publique el 15 de marzo.

examples.en: The Prime Minister is to visit Madrid next week.
examples.es: Está previsto que el primer ministro visite Madrid la semana que viene.

explain.title: 5 · El futuro visto desde el pasado
explain.es: Cuando narramos o contamos lo que alguien pensaba, el futuro retrocede: will → would, am going to → was going to, is about to → was about to. was/were going to se usa mucho para planes que no se cumplieron (iba a…, pero). En narración formal, was/were to + infinitivo expresa el destino, lo que acabaría pasando (llegaría a…), y was/were to have + participio, un plan frustrado (tenía que haber…).
explain.en: In narratives the future shifts back: would, was going to, was about to. Was going to often signals an unfulfilled plan. Formal narrative: was to (destiny) and was to have + participle (a plan that did not happen).

examples.en: I was going to email you, but the server went down.
examples.es: Iba a escribirte un correo, pero se cayó el servidor.

examples.en: She knew that the decision would change her life.
examples.es: Sabía que la decisión le cambiaría la vida.

examples.en: We were about to leave when the client called.
examples.es: Estábamos a punto de irnos cuando llamó el cliente.

examples.en: He was to become one of the finest architects of his generation.
examples.es: Llegaría a ser uno de los mejores arquitectos de su generación.

examples.en: The bridge was to have opened in 2020, but funding ran out.
examples.es: El puente tenía que haberse inaugurado en 2020, pero se acabó la financiación.

explain.title: Expresiones de inminencia y previsión
head: Expresión
Significado
Registro
Ejemplo
rows: I was just about to call you!
She was on the point of resigning.
The species is on the verge of extinction.
The country is on the brink of recession.
The flight is due to land at 10.15.
explain.note: Cuidado: due to + infinitivo = previsto (The train is due to arrive), pero due to + nombre = debido a (The delay was due to fog).
explain.note_en: due to + infinitive = scheduled; due to + noun = because of.

explain.title: ¿Se cumplió o no?
explain.es: En el futuro en el pasado, la estructura elegida suele indicar si el plan se cumplió o se quedó en nada.
explain.en: The structure often tells us whether the plan came true.

cols.head: ❌ No se cumplió
items: I was going to study medicine, but I changed my mind.
The talks were to have taken place in Geneva.
We were about to sign when the deal collapsed.

cols.head: ✅ Sí se cumplió
items: Nobody imagined that she would one day lead the party.
This concert was to be his last.
Ten years later, the village would become a tourist hotspot.

explain.title: Oraciones temporales: sin will
head: Conector
Tras el conector
Oración principal
Ejemplo
rows: When you arrive, we'll be waiting for you.
By the time she retires, she'll have taught for 40 years.
Once we've signed the contract, we'll announce it.
We won't know until the results come out.
After you've read it, you'll understand.
explain.note: Error típico por calco del subjuntivo español (cuando llegues, para cuando termine): When you will arrive → When you arrive. Tampoco when I will have finished → when I've finished.
explain.note_en: Never use will (or will have) after time conjunctions: use the present or present perfect.

items.bad: By the time you will arrive, we'll have left.
items.good: By the time you arrive, we'll have left.
items.why: Tras by the time / when / until → presente, no will.

items.bad: This time tomorrow I will fly to Berlin.
items.good: This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Berlin.
items.why: Acción en curso en un momento futuro → will be + -ing.
items.why_en: In progress at a future time → future continuous.

items.bad: Until Friday I'll have finished the report.
items.good: By Friday I'll have finished the report.

items.bad: Next year I'll have been knowing her for 20 years.
items.good: Next year I'll have known her for 20 years.
items.why: Know es verbo de estado: sin forma continua.
items.why_en: State verbs have no continuous form.

items.bad: The train is about to leave in ten minutes.
items.good: The train is due to leave in ten minutes.
items.why: About to = inminente: no admite expresión de tiempo.
items.why_en: about to takes no time expression.

items.bad: We are on the point to sign the deal.
items.good: We are on the point of signing the deal.

items.bad: I knew it will be difficult.
items.why: Futuro visto desde el pasado → would.

items.bad: In June I'll be working here for five years.
items.good: In June I'll have been working here for five years.
items.why: Duración hasta un momento futuro → will have been + -ing.
items.why_en: Duration up to a future point.

items.es: ¿Hablas de un momento concreto del futuro y la acción estará a medias? → will be + -ing.
items.en: In progress at a future moment → will be + -ing.

items.es: ¿Estará terminada antes de un límite (by…)? → will have + participio.
items.en: Finished before a deadline → will have + participle.

items.es: ¿Importa cuánto tiempo llevará (for…)? → will have been + -ing (o la forma simple si es un verbo de estado).
items.en: Duration → will have been + -ing (simple with state verbs).

items.es: ¿Es inminente? → be about to (sin hora). ¿Está en un horario? → be due to (+ hora).
items.en: Imminent → be about to; scheduled → be due to.

items.es: ¿Narras en pasado? → retrocede: would, was going to, was about to, was to.
items.en: Narrating in the past → would, was going to, was about to, was to.

items.es: Revisa: tras when, by the time, until, as soon as no hay will.
items.en: Check: no will after time conjunctions.

lines.en: So, where will we be with the launch by the end of the month?
lines.es: Bueno, ¿en qué punto estaremos con el lanzamiento a final de mes?

lines.en: By then we'll have finished the beta testing, and the design team will be working on the final tweaks.
lines.es: Para entonces habremos terminado las pruebas beta y el equipo de diseño estará con los últimos retoques.

lines.en: Good. The investors are due to visit on the 28th. Will you be presenting the demo?
lines.es: Bien. Está previsto que los inversores vengan el día 28. ¿Vas a presentar tú la demo?

lines.en: I was going to ask Priya, but she'll be attending a conference in Lisbon that week.
lines.es: Iba a pedírselo a Priya, pero esa semana estará en un congreso en Lisboa.

lines.en: Then it'll have to be you. By the 28th you'll have been working on this for eight months — nobody knows it better.
lines.es: Entonces tendrás que ser tú. Para el 28 llevarás ocho meses trabajando en esto: nadie lo conoce mejor.

lines.en: Fair enough. Actually, I was just about to send you the updated schedule.
lines.es: Vale. De hecho, estaba a punto de enviarte el calendario actualizado.

lines.en: Perfect. As soon as I've read it, I'll forward it to the board.
lines.es: Perfecto. En cuanto lo haya leído, se lo reenviaré al consejo.

lines.en: Great. I'll be waiting for your feedback.
lines.es: Genial. Quedo a la espera de tus comentarios.

explain.title: Truco de la máquina del tiempo
explain.es: Viaja mentalmente a ese momento del futuro y pregúntate: ¿Qué estoy haciendo? → will be + -ing. ¿Qué ya he hecho? → will have + participio. ¿Cuánto tiempo llevo? → will have been + -ing. Es la misma lógica que el present continuous, el present perfect y el present perfect continuous… ¡pero trasladada al futuro con will!
explain.en: Travel mentally to that future moment and ask: What am I doing? What have I done? How long have I been doing it? Then add will.

items.q: “By the time you arrive, I'll have cooked dinner.” → Dinner will be ready when you arrive.
“When you arrive, I'll be cooking dinner.” → Dinner will be ready when you arrive.
items.why: Estaré cocinando: la cena aún no estará lista.

items.q: “In May she'll have been teaching for 30 years.” → She is still teaching now.
items.why: La forma continua indica que la actividad sigue.

items.q: “I was going to apply for the post.” → I applied for the post.
items.why: Was going to = plan que no se cumplió.

items.q: “The train is due to leave at 10.” → The train has already left.
“He was to become prime minister.” → He did become prime minister.
“The ceremony was to have taken place in May.” → The ceremony took place in May.
items.why: Was to have + participio = plan frustrado.

items.q: “They'll have landed by now.” → The speaker thinks they have probably landed.
items.why: Future perfect = suposición sobre el presente.

items.a: By next week I'll have known about this for a month.

items.a: This time tomorrow we'll be sitting our final exam.

items.a: By Friday the decorators will have finished.

items.a: The concert is due to start in half an hour.

items.a: We were on the point of giving up when we found the solution.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el artículo. Marca T (verdadero) o F (falso) y contesta las preguntas con frases completas.
exercises.en: Read the article. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
exercises.text_title: Countdown to the new Science Museum
text: When the new Science Museum opens its doors in September, it will have been under construction for almost seven years. The project was originally due to open in 2024, but, as it turned out, the opening was to be postponed twice. At one stage the council was on the point of cancelling the scheme altogether.

Now the end is finally in sight. By the end of this month, the builders will have installed the last of the glass panels, and in July the curators will be moving more than 10,000 objects into the galleries. “We're about to enter the most exciting phase,” says the director, Helen Marsh. “By opening day, my team will have been working on the exhibitions for over three years.”

Not everyone is impressed. Critics point out that, by the time the museum opens, the budget will have doubled. Marsh, however, remains confident: “I always knew this project would be difficult. But in twenty years' time, nobody will be talking about the delays — they'll be talking about the museum.”

items.q: The museum was originally due to open in 2024.
The council cancelled the project at one stage.
items.why: It was on the point of cancelling it, but it didn't.

items.q: The last glass panels will be in place by the end of this month.
What will the curators be doing in July?
items.a: They will be moving more than 10,000 objects into the galleries.

items.q: How long will Helen Marsh's team have been working on the exhibitions by opening day?
What will have happened to the budget by the time the museum opens?
Find two examples of the future seen from the past.
items.a: “the opening was to be postponed twice” and “I always knew this project would be difficult”.

items.q: Helen Marsh thinks people will remember the museum for its delays.
items.why: She thinks they'll be talking about the museum, not the delays.

exercises.title: Traduce al inglés
exercises.es: Traduce. Piensa: ¿en curso, terminado, duración, inminente o futuro desde el pasado?

items.q: Mañana a estas horas estaré entrevistando al ministro.
items.a: This time tomorrow I'll be interviewing the minister.

items.q: Para cuando llegues, ya habremos cenado.
a: By the time you arrive, we'll have had dinner.
By the time you get here, we'll have eaten.

items.q: En septiembre llevaré cinco años viviendo en Edimburgo.
items.a: In September I'll have been living in Edinburgh for five years.

items.q: Está previsto que el vuelo aterrice a las 22:15.
items.a: The flight is due to land at 22.15.

items.q: (Él) estaba a punto de dimitir cuando le ofrecieron el puesto.
a: He was on the point of resigning when they offered him the post.
He was about to resign when he was offered the post.

items.q: Iba a llamarte, pero se me olvidó.
items.a: I was going to call you, but I forgot.

items.q: ¿Vas a usar el portátil esta tarde? (pregunta cortés)
items.a: Will you be using the laptop this afternoon?

items.q: Ya te habrás enterado de la noticia.
Sabía que no sería fácil.
items.a: I knew it wouldn't be easy.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Escribe frases sobre ti con las estructuras de este mapa.
exercises.en: Write about yourself using the structures in this map.

items.q: ¿Qué estarás haciendo mañana a estas horas y dentro de diez años? (will be + -ing)
items.a: Ej.: This time tomorrow I'll be giving a presentation. In ten years' time I'll be running my own consultancy.

items.q: Escribe tres cosas que habrás conseguido para final de año. (By the end of the year…)
items.a: Ej.: By the end of the year I'll have passed my C1 exam, paid off my car and run a half marathon.

items.q: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevarás haciendo algo importante para ti el próximo verano? (will have been + -ing)
items.a: Ej.: Next summer I'll have been playing the cello for fifteen years.

items.q: Cuenta un plan que no se cumplió y por qué. (was going to… but)
items.a: Ej.: I was going to move to Dublin last year, but my company offered me a promotion.

checklist.es: Uso will be + -ing para acciones en curso en el futuro y para preguntas corteses.
checklist.en: I can use the future continuous for actions in progress and polite questions.

checklist.es: Uso will have + participio con by para lo que estará terminado.
checklist.en: I can use the future perfect with by for completed actions.

checklist.es: Uso will have been + -ing para la duración (y la forma simple con verbos de estado).
checklist.en: I can use the future perfect continuous for duration.

checklist.es: Distingo be about to, be on the point of, be due to y be set to.
checklist.en: I can distinguish about to, on the point of, due to and set to.

checklist.es: Hablo del futuro desde el pasado con would, was going to, was to.
checklist.en: I can talk about the future in the past.

checklist.es: Nunca pongo <s>will</s> después de when, by the time, until o as soon as.
checklist.en: I never use will after time conjunctions.
